purpose: Distinguish loss of delivered video-frame history from an unproven erroneous cadence lock in the existing phase-candidate result. No new playback run.

method.counterDelta: Last minus first cumulative stats sample; not the complete 60-second window.
method.intervalDelta: stats[i] minus stats[i-1]; endingMode is sampled only at i, not throughout the interval.
method.qualityDelta: Independent video quality snapshots at the start and end of the complete measurement.

codeEvidence.missedMeaning: #count adds max(0, presentedFrames - lastPresented - 1) outside a timestamp discontinuity. Counts frames skipped between callbacks, not the number of callbacks.
codeEvidence.historyReset: When autoFilm is enabled and presentedFrames advances by more than one, #frames is cleared and #resetFilm runs (lines 742-751).
codeEvidence.degradedMeaning: #render increments degraded when the three-frame history is unavailable or a flush is requested.

conclusions: The anomalous candidate run accumulates missed frames in all 57 observed intervals; the three other starts have no missed increment.
The same anomalous run adds 1208 degraded renders, while the other three starts add none.
All five runs add 20 to the browser dropped-video counter; that counter alone does not distinguish the anomalous run.
The unsuccessful candidate remains unadopted. Erroneous phase lock is not established; frame-history reset is another code-backed mechanism requiring per-callback diagnosis.
limitations: No per-callback presentedFrames or input callback count was recorded.
One-second stats cannot establish event ordering inside each interval or identify why callbacks skipped frames.
These are the already measured builds, not new evidence for the current integration or Starlette candidate.
